Commentary.Commentary: The Windies batters will now have to put in a special performance if they are to have a chance. They have not batted that well so far in the series but they need to come good here. South Africa on the other hand, will hope to take a few wickets before Lunch.

For the Windies, they were brilliant at the start of the innings, their pacers were just really good and they had the hosts in trouble but as the day went on, they just were not as consistent as they were earlier on Day 3 and they just let the game slip away. The spinners were quite disappointing. Had they bowled better on a wicket which was offering turn, things could have well been different.

South Africa have just the one man to thank for the position they are in, in this game and it is their skipper! Take his innings out and Windies would probably been on top. Let me remind you, they were struggling at 103 for 5 with the lead then, below 200 but Wiaan Mulder and Temba Bavuma put up a really good stand and that put South Africa on top and then the stand between Simon Harmer and Temba Bavuma probably has taken the game away from the Windies. The Day 4 morning did not go as South Africa wanted but because of the knock from their skipper, they are well ahead in this game.

Temba Bavuma was the most relieved man on Day 3 as he notched up his second Test hundred and not just for him but it was a vital knock for his team. South Africa were 32 for 3 but the skipper stepped up and played a blistering knock to help his team get a lead above 350. He is still unbeaten and if West Indies do not clean the tail quickly they will be looking for a big score to chase. The first session is going to be very vital. Stay tuned.
...Day 4, Session 1...

West Indies have to gather some energy if they want to keep South Africa below 400. Before thinking to bat, they need to take the remaining wickets quickly. Bavuma though will now look for double-hundred. Join us for the action of Day 4 at 1330 IST (0800 GMT) and earlier for the build up. Till then, cheers!

The first thing South Africa will look is to extend their lead over 400 which might prove just too much for the Windies. West Indies were lazy as the game progressed. Kraigg Brathwaite tried everything but were just not able to get past Bavuma who stand like a rock. In the final minutes, Jason Holder did got Harmer but it was not enough as the damage was happening from the other side

A day that belongs to South Africa and their captain as they extend the lead over 350. A top, top innings from Bavuma who's grit and determination meant very tough for the Windies to break. South Africa are in a really good position to win this game. From the start, they kept on losing wickets but Temba Bavuma hold his crease from one end and got support form Wiaan Mulder and then with Simon Harmer. The skipper was relentless and turned up in the final session as South Africa scored at a quick rate.

South Africa on the other hand, are effectively 138 for 4. They would know one good partnership is all they need. Their skipper is set and they would expect him to play long but he will need someone to hang around with him. An interesting session awaits. Stay tuned.

What a session for the Windies. They have managed to take 4 wickets in it and have kept themselves well and truly alive in the game. The key for them was the discipline the pacers bowled with. Kyle Mayers and Jason Holder were brilliant to begin with. Holder kept it tight and Mayers got two to begin with. Raymon Reifer and Kemar Roach then continued the good work and both got a wicket each too. More of the same is what the away side will want after the break.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! A wicket just before the break, exactly what Windies wanted! Raymon Reifer strikes! Length and just outside off, Ryan Rickelton did not need to go after that one but he does. It goes off the outside edge and it is taken by the keeper. Ryan Rickelton walks back and so do all the players as it is LUNCH!
Commentary.Howout: c Joshua Da Silva b Raymon Reifer

South Africa passed the hurdle of playing a few overs on Day 2 and have a lead of 73 runs. South Africa are in good position but have to bat for probably full day or so to have a chance to win. The pitch is assisting the bowlers and West Indies will look to keep the score as low as possible. West Indies will be gutted the way they batted. They had a real chance to cut out the lead but apart from Jason Holder no one stepped up. Now though, West Indies have to bowl with discipline and accurate and get wickets regularly. Let's hope Day 3 is as interesting as this game had been till now.
....Day 3, Session 1...

Right then, that is it from the Day 2 of the game. The hosts have their noses in front at the moment but some quick wickets at the start can get the visitors back into the game. Can they do it? Or will the hosts continue to bat freely and put up a mammoth total on the board? To find out, join us at 1.30 pm IST (8.00 am GMT) and earlier for the build-up of Day 3. Cheers!

West Indies were curtailed to 28 for 3 courtesy of some tight-pace bowling from the Proteas. They kept on losing wickets at regular intervals. Jason Holder was the only batter who stood firm for them as he played an unbeaten knock of 81 runs. They were finally bundled out for 251 runs. They will be hoping for some quick wickets now and claw their way back into the game. It will be interesting to see how the visitors respond with the ball.

The home side started the day on 311 and was soon bundled out in three overs. They ended their innings at 320. They were excellent with the ball when the visitors come to bat and picked up quick wickets. They took a bit of time to pick the last wicket as Jason Holder and Gudakesh Motie stitched a partnership of 58 runs at the end and reduced the lead to 69 runs. They will be the happier side going into Day 3 as they have a lead of 73 runs.

That is it, Day 2 comes to a close and it is South Africa who is in the driver's seat at the moment. They have a lead of 73 runs and they will look to stretch their lead and post a mammoth total on the board. West Indies will hope to get some quick wickets and get back into the game.
